subject: Reachability and retained-body review of the folded EventView cache candidate
decision: Do not implement or merge the proposed cache patch on this evidence.

source_findings.finding: The production activity view sets EventScope::Conversation before calling EventView::render. The Logs view renders the raw VT log, not the EventView All-scope detail branch.
Native file-read audit events retain path, offsets and byte counts, not file bodies.
Ordinary file-read and skill-read display branches emit one-line path summaries. This is not a universal bound on all interleaved pending renderer text.
Read details retain the full safe source and path and remove the existing summary heading. The real measured read records contain no document bodies.
Expanded read-group members retain derived row caches after folding. The identified behavior is real, but this probe does not show a large resident body or a physical-memory benefit from changing it.

interpretation: The same unmodified CLI produced all phases. Phase differences are not a baseline-versus-candidate comparison.
Twelve 2048-byte documents produced only 720 retained display bytes across twelve read records.
The four loaded-state foreground PSS medians span 32 KiB. This does not establish savings from a cache patch.
No event, archive, history, retention limit or production configuration was changed.
The initial Logs/All measurement idea was rejected after tracing actual production callers.
Freeing an internal Vec allocation would not by itself prove lower RSS or PSS; an appropriate same-profile A/B would still be required for such a claim.
scope_limits: This ordinary twelve-document workload does not prove a global upper bound for every legal long path or interleaved renderer state.
No increased workload or synthetic retained file body was used to manufacture an optimization claim.
This record is a diagnostic decision, not completion of the user request for lower steady-state memory.
